statuses.name: invalid
statuses.summary: The request or its arguments are invalid.

statuses.name: stale
statuses.summary: No screen is open, or the screen is no longer current.

statuses.name: busy
statuses.summary: The device can't take this request now; try again later.

statuses.name: no_memory
statuses.summary: The device ran out of memory for this request.

statuses.name: denied
statuses.summary: The plugin may not do this: a missing grant, or a destination the device refuses.

statuses.name: unavailable
statuses.summary: Not available now or on this device: no SD card, or the screen isn't visible.

statuses.name: limit
statuses.summary: A rate, size or storage limit was reached.

statuses.name: failed
statuses.summary: The device tried and failed: network error, timeout, TLS error.

errors.summary: Malformed request, or an argument is missing, of the wrong type, out of range or too long.
The device doesn't know this capability or operation.
system.hello must be the first request.
The device doesn't support this protocol or API version.
hello claimed an id other than the one the device started; the plugin is stopped.
An HTTP header is malformed, or one the device sets itself (Host, Content-Length, Connection, Transfer-Encoding, Proxy-*).
The package has no sounds/<name>.wav.
The sound isn't a 16 kHz, mono, 16-bit PCM WAV file within the size limit.
The stream rate isn't one the speaker plays: 8000, 11025, 12000, 16000, 22050, 24000, 32000, 44100 or 48000 Hz.
No screen is open.
An HTTP request is already running; wait for its result.
An alarm, a call or the voice assistant holds the speaker, or another plugin is streaming (D28).
The plugin's audio stream is open; sounds wait until it closes.
The device ran out of memory.
plugin.json doesn't list the capability this operation needs in requested_capabilities.
The URL isn't http or https, or its host resolves to a loopback, private, link-local or other non-public address.
Sound plays only while the plugin's screen is visible.
The plugin has no working audio channel: it doesn't hold audio.stream, or an earlier malformed frame ended the channel for this run (D28).
Plugin storage isn't available: no SD card, or it can't be written.
Too many requests of this kind; slow down.
Plugin storage is full.
The result is larger than the plugin can receive.
The HTTP request didn't finish in time.
DNS, connection or transfer failure.
The server's TLS certificate couldn't be verified.
Only a firmware feature module (D25) may use this operation.
The plugin already holds the most scheduler entries it may: 8 for a firmware module, 4 for a community plugin.
Another entry of this plugin is due within 5 minutes of this one (community plugins, D26).
The owner hasn't turned on "Allow alarms" for this plugin on the Device Console (D26).
No entry of this plugin is due to ring now.

grants.name: ui
grants.summary: Show the plugin's own screens and update them.

grants.name: storage
grants.summary: Keep small text values across runs, in a store only this plugin can reach. Needs an SD card.

grants.name: http
grants.summary: Make HTTP and HTTPS requests to public internet hosts. Local network, loopback and reserved addresses are refused.

grants.name: audio.output
grants.summary: Play tones and the package's own sounds on the speaker, only while the plugin's screen is visible.

grants.name: schedule
grants.summary: Ring the device at set times, with the entry's label and a built-in sound; the device shows its own alarm screen, titled with the plugin's name. A community plugin needs the owner's "Allow alarms" on the Device Console (D26) and holds at most 4 entries, 5 minutes apart.

grants.name: settings
grants.summary: Keep the module's settings on internal flash. Firmware feature modules only (D25).

grants.name: status
grants.summary: Publish the module's status for the device and other modules. Firmware feature modules only (D25).

grants.name: idle.face
grants.summary: Fill in the plugin's idle face (D22), the home screen face the owner may choose on the Device Console.

grants.name: audio.stream
grants.summary: Stream continuous audio to the speaker, such as a radio or a podcast, only while the plugin's screen is visible (D28). Alarms, calls and the voice assistant pause it.

grants.name: audio.background
grants.summary: Keep an audio stream playing after the plugin's screen closes (D29). Firmware feature modules only; the owner stops it with LEFT long press.

grants.name: net
grants.summary: Open the module's own TCP and TLS connections to public addresses, outside the broker (D30). Firmware feature modules only, and only where the target's kernel gate is installed.

ops.summary: Opens a compiled screen. With wait_ms, waits up to that long for the device to become idle (voice start, D11).
Sets a bound value on the open screen.
Closes the open screen.

Opens one of the device's screen templates with the plugin's text (D27): status (title, optional emoji, an OK button), alert (an icon, title, OK) or menu (title and 1 to 4 items). RIGHT on OK gives the action template.ok; RIGHT on item N gives template.itemN. Like open, it replaces the plugin's screen, waits like open with wait_ms, and is preempted by the device.
Reads a value. The result has found (true or false) and value.
Stores a text value under a key, replacing any earlier value. Values may contain tabs and newlines, but no other control characters.
Removes a key. Removing a missing key succeeds.
Lists the stored keys. The result has keys, an array of strings.
Makes one HTTP request and returns status, content_type, body (text, cut to fit) and truncated. Redirects are returned, not followed. One request at a time.
Plays a sine tone, replacing any sound playing. A sound_done event follows.
Plays sounds/<sound>.wav from the package (16 kHz, mono, 16-bit PCM, at most 10 s), replacing any sound playing. A sound_done event follows.
Stops the sound playing, if any.

Opens the plugin's audio stream at rate Hz (D28): 16-bit mono PCM frames then go on the audio channel (aitbase_audio_stream_write). Stops any sound playing. stream_state events follow. background (D29, audio.background) keeps it playing after the screen closes; it needs no screen, and title names it on the core's screen after the package's name.
Plays out the frames already sent, then closes the stream. A stream_state event with state stopped and reason closed follows.
Adds or replaces the plugin's entry with this id. A ringing entry makes the device ring at due_epoch with its label, even if the plugin isn't running then (D23).
Removes the plugin's entry with this id. The result has found.
The plugin's own entries: entries is a list of {id, due_epoch, rings, label}.
Rings the entry that schedule.due just announced, with its label. Without it the device rings anyway after a short grace period (C14).
The module's settings: found, and values, an object of string values.
Replaces the module's settings: at most 64 keys of [a-z0-9_] up to 32 bytes, string values up to 512 bytes.
Removes the module's settings.
Publishes a status value under the module's own prefix: key is <module>.<name>.

Sets a value of the plugin's idle face (D22): the labels its face document binds to key. The device keeps the values, so the face shows them after a reboot without the plugin running. Works whether or not the owner has chosen the face.

events.summary: The open was refused, cancelled by another device state, or timed out. data.detail says why.
The screen was closed after a close request.
The device took the screen back: LEFT long press, voice assistant, settings. Any sound stops.
The user activated a focusable widget with RIGHT. data.node and data.action.

A button was pressed while the plugin's screen shows: LEFT press, RIGHT press or RIGHT long press (a long press comes after a press of the same button). data.key is left or right, data.gesture is press or long_press. LEFT long press is never delivered: it leaves the plugin.
An update was refused when the device applied it. data.node and data.detail.
The sound started by data.request finished, was replaced or stopped. data.detail is finished, stopped or failed.

The audio stream changed (D28). data.state is paused (an alarm, a call or the assistant took the speaker; frames wait), resumed, or stopped, with data.reason: closed, preempted (the screen closed), replaced (music or another stream started), idle_timeout (no frame for 10 s), bad_stream (a malformed frame, or a frame while no stream is open; the channel stays closed for this run) or failed (the speaker failed). user means LEFT long press ended a background stream (D29).
An entry of this plugin is due. data.id names it; ring it with schedule.ring if it rings.
A declared action of the module's screen. data.action is snooze or stop.
